slides.title: What *counts*
slides.body: Double charges, the wrong amount, things you never got, returns that were never credited, and charges you do not recognize. This is a US law, the Fair Credit Billing Act.

slides.title: Watch the *clock*
slides.body: Ask the seller for a refund first. But your 60 days start from the first statement that showed the charge, and they keep running while you wait.

slides.title: Put it *in writing*
slides.body: Calling is fine, but a letter keeps your rights. Send it to the billing inquiries address on your statement, not the payment address. Use tracked mail and keep a copy.

slides.title: Let *Claude* write it
slides.body: Paste the charge and what went wrong, then ask: Write a short billing error letter to my card company with the charge, the date and why it is wrong. Leave a blank for my account number.

slides.title: What *happens next*
slides.body: They must confirm your letter within 30 days and settle it within 2 billing cycles, never more than 90 days. You can hold the disputed amount. Pay the rest on time.
